skill.name: convention-learner
skill.description: Guides analysis of .NET project conventions, including naming, folder structure, testing, and coding style, to support consistent code generation and review.
skill.summary: Identify evidence-based .NET coding conventions and apply them during code generation and review.
skill.author: codewithmukesh

content.value_statement: Inconsistent naming and structure make existing .NET projects harder to extend and review. This skill guides evidence-based convention discovery and applies findings to code suggestions.
actual_capabilities: Guides project graph and public API inspection to identify naming, architecture, and type-modifier conventions.
Examines folder organization and explicit settings in .editorconfig, Directory.Build.props, and global.json.
Compiles observed naming, structure, and code-style patterns into a convention summary.
Applies detected conventions to code-generation suggestions and flags deviations during review.
Suggests EditorConfig rules and CLAUDE.md documentation based on observed evidence.
Uses detect_antipatterns results to prioritize recurring quality issues and compare available counts.
limitations: Provides instructions only; it does not bundle an executable analyzer or the referenced MCP tools.
Focuses on .NET and C# projects; examples may not transfer directly to other languages.
Sampled types can miss exceptions; reliable conclusions require confirmation across representative files.
Cross-session trend comparison and instinct promotion depend on external tools or skills not included here.

use_cases.title: Understand an Existing Codebase
use_cases.description: Inspect representative types, folder layouts, and configuration to summarize conventions before implementing a first change.

use_cases.title: Review Convention Deviations
use_cases.description: Compare changed handlers and DTOs against observed project patterns, distinguishing explicit rules from inferred preferences.

use_cases.title: Document Team Standards
use_cases.description: Turn repeated code patterns and quality findings into proposed convention documentation and EditorConfig settings.

prompt_templates.title: Find Basic Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this .NET project and summarize naming, folder organization, and coding style. Cite representative files and distinguish confirmed patterns from uncertain observations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Consistent Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review existing features before planning [feature]. Identify matching folders, handler modifiers, DTO styles, and configuration rules. Propose an implementation outline without editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a feature that matches existing code.

prompt_templates.title: Review Changed Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the changed files with representative project code and explicit configuration. Report convention deviations with evidence and suggested fixes. Do not treat exceptions as universal rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess consistency during code review.

prompt_templates.title: Propose Evidence-Based Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze representative layers and available anti-pattern results. Separate explicit rules from inferred patterns, compare supplied historical counts, and propose CLAUDE.md and EditorConfig changes for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: consolidate standards and recurring quality findings.

output_examples.input: Summarize conventions from a supplied sample of five handlers and existing project settings.
output: Naming: All five inspected handlers use the Handler suffix.
Modifiers: All five sampled handlers are internal and sealed; confirm other modules before making this a project-wide rule.
Configuration: The supplied settings require file-scoped namespaces.
Recommendation: Document these findings and inspect additional layers before enforcing inferred rules.

output_examples.input: Review a public handler when twelve comparable handlers are internal and sealed.
output: Deviation: The new handler is public, while all twelve comparable handlers are internal and sealed.
Suggested change: Match the existing modifiers unless this handler has a documented accessibility requirement.
Follow-up: Record the confirmed convention in team documentation after review.

best_practices: Inspect several representative files across layers before documenting an inferred convention.
Give explicit .editorconfig and Directory.Build.props rules precedence over inferred style preferences.
Review proposed documentation and configuration changes before applying them to the repository.
anti_patterns: Imposing generic handler modifiers or folder layouts without examining the existing project.
Treating a pattern observed in one file as a universal team standard.
Claiming historical trends or automatic enforcement without the required tools and supporting evidence.

faq.question: Which projects does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets .NET and C# projects, including their naming, folder structure, configuration, and testing conventions.

faq.question: Does the skill include analysis tools?
faq.answer: No. It references get_project_graph, get_public_api, and detect_antipatterns, but does not bundle their implementations.

faq.question: Can it enforce conventions automatically?
faq.answer: It guides consistent code suggestions and review. Proposed EditorConfig rules require compatible tooling and adoption before they provide automated enforcement.

faq.question: What happens when existing settings conflict with inferred conventions?
faq.answer: Explicit .editorconfig and Directory.Build.props rules take precedence over inferred patterns and generic defaults.

faq.question: Can it track quality trends across sessions?
faq.answer: It describes comparing anti-pattern counts. Reliable trends require retained results or external tooling; the skill itself supplies no storage.

faq.question: Will it rewrite the entire repository?
faq.answer: It describes analysis, code-generation guidance, review, and proposed documentation updates. It does not include a bulk migration script.
